Hello Earl,

While further experimenting - I see hep tells me: " If words are
split that shouldn't be, users can give a character class to specify
word characters".

Here is the code I've been using. How would ensure only whole words
are counted using 'word_char' and with ngram_freq is it possible to
exclude numbers and output like 10PM or 10TH ?


X <- load_txt('D://Rodger/MyTW/')
output <- concord(X, "instead", shorten = 25)
write.csv(output,"D://TEST2.csv")


ngram_freq(X, num_wd = 2, ignore_case = TRUE, order_by = "alpha",
descending = FALSE, min_freq = 10)


Regards

Bob

messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: corpling R package # 2
parts:
I think your question deals with regular expressions (or regexes). You can specify word boundaries in a regex with "\\b", so for example, in concord() you would specify "\\binstead\\b". Again, "\\b" is a locale-specific thing, so if that doesn't give you what you want, you may need to specify the exact character that shouldn't be considered word characters. See QCLWR p. 84. You may want to review section 3.7.5, starting on p. 79. Stefan gives a thorough run-down of regular expressions in that section.

Best of luck.
